list_1.title: Creating a list
list_1.prompt: What symbol do we use to create a list in Python?
list_1.explanation: Lists use square brackets [ ]! frutas = ["maçã", "banana"] stores two fruits in a list! 📋

list_2.title: First item is zero
list_2.prompt: In Python, the first item in a list has position 0 (not 1).
list_2.explanation: Python starts from zero! frutas[0] is the first item, frutas[1] is the second. 🎯

list_3.title: Get the second item
list_3.explanation: Position 0 is maçã, position 1 is banana, position 2 is laranja! 🍌

list_4.title: Add to list
list_4.prompt: Which method adds an item to the end of the list?
list_4.explanation: append() adds to the end! frutas.append("uva") puts uva at the end of the list! ➕

list_5.title: Count evens in list
list_5.prompt: Create a function that counts how many even numbers are in the list.
list_5.explanation: Use for to go through each number. If numero % 2 == 0, it's even! Count how many there are. 🔢

list_6.title: List Size
list_6.prompt: What command tells how many items are in the list `[10, 20, 30]`?
list_6.explanation: len() stands for length. It counts how many items are in the list. len([10, 20, 30]) gives 3! 📏

list_slice_1.title: Slicing the List
list_slice_1.prompt: What does lista[1:3] return from the list ["a", "b", "c", "d"]?
list_slice_1.explanation: lista[1:3] gets from index 1 until before 3! It's like slicing a cake 🎂 - index 1 is "b" and index 2 is "c".

list_slice_2.title: Getting the First Ones
list_slice_2.prompt: Complete to get the first 2 numbers:
list_slice_2.explanation: [0:2] gets from the beginning (0) until before 2, meaning indices 0 and 1! ✂️

list_pop_1.title: Removing and Getting
list_pop_1.explanation: pop() takes the last item from the list and gives it to you! It's like drawing the last card from the deck. 🃏
options: Removes and returns the last item
Adds an item at the end

list_sort_1.title: Sorting the List
list_sort_1.prompt: The method lista.sort() puts the numbers in ascending order.
list_sort_1.explanation: That's it! sort() organizes the list! [3, 1, 2] becomes [1, 2, 3]. Very useful! 📊

list_remove_1.title: Removing by Value
list_remove_1.prompt: Complete to remove "banana" from the list:
list_remove_1.explanation: remove() takes the item out by value! Tell the item's name and it vanishes from the list. 🍌❌

list_7.title: Shopping List
list_7.prompt: Add "leite" to the shopping list using append:
list_7.explanation: append() glues the item to the end of the list! Now "leite" is part of the groceries! 🛒

list_8.title: How many colors?
list_8.prompt: Use `len` to find out how many colors are in the list:
list_8.explanation: len() counts how many items are in the list! It's like counting on your fingers: one, two, three colors! 🎨

list_iter_1.title: Walking through the List
list_iter_1.prompt: Which loop is better to go through each item in a list?
list_iter_1.explanation: We use `for item in lista` to visit each item, one by one! It's like a roll call in the classroom. 📢

list_iter_2.title: Showing the Fruits
list_iter_2.prompt: Complete the loop to show each fruit in the list:
list_iter_2.explanation: `in` means inside or in. For each fruit IN the list of fruits, show the fruit! 🍎🍐

list_9.title: Removing the First
list_9.prompt: How do we remove the FIRST item of a list called `cores`?
list_9.explanation: pop() without a number takes the last one. But if you tell the index, it takes that specific one! pop(0) takes the item at position 0 (the first one). 1️⃣

list_10.title: Reverse Order
list_10.prompt: How do we sort a list from largest to smallest?
list_10.explanation: sort() organizes from smallest to largest. To invert it (largest to smallest), we use the reverse=True option! 🔄

list_11.title: Summing the List
list_11.prompt: Use `sum()` to sum all numbers in the list:
list_11.explanation: `sum()` is a magic function that adds up everything in the list! 10 + 20 + 30 = 60. Super fast! ➕

list_12.title: Adding Colors
list_12.prompt: Which command adds the color "Roxo" at the end of the list `cores`?
list_12.explanation: append("Roxo") adds the item at the end of the list. It's like adding another wagon to the train! 🚂

list_13.title: Getting the Middle
list_13.explanation: It gets from index 2 (number 2) until BEFORE index 4 (number 4). So it gets 2 and 3! The 4 is left out! 🍰

list_14.title: Popping Balloons
list_14.explanation: `pop()` pops (removes) the LAST item of the list. Bye bye, blue balloon! 🎈

list_15.title: Organizing Points
list_15.prompt: Put the list of points in ascending order (from smallest to largest):
list_15.explanation: `sort()` organizes the mess! It puts numbers in ascending order (1, 2, 3) or letters in alphabetical order (A, B, C). 📊

list_16.title: Backpack Full?
list_16.prompt: Find out how many items are in the backpack using `len()`:
list_16.explanation: `len()` counts everything for you! It's super useful to know if the backpack is full or if there's room for more. 🎒

boss_battle_7.title: The Organizing Giant
boss_battle_7.prompt: The Giant has a list [5, 2, 8, 1]. Sort the list and show it!
boss_battle_7.explanation: The Giant is messy! Use sort() to organize the list! 🗿
